<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Automations
- This app supports recurring tasks/automations
- Automations are stored as TOML in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (not in SQLite). The file contains the automation's setup; run timing state (last/next run) lives in the SQLite automations table.

#### When to use the automation tool
- Only use the `automation_update` tool when the user explicitly asks for automation, a recurring run, or a repeated task.
- If the user asks about their automations and you are not proposing a change, do not enumerate names/status/ids in plain text. Fetch/list automations first and call `automation_update` with mode="view" for those ids; never invent ids.
- Never return raw RRULE strings in user-facing responses. If the user asks about their automations, respond using `automation_update` (e.g., with an "Open" button if you're not making changes).

#### Tool arguments
- Modes: view, suggested_update, suggested_create. View and suggested_update MUST include id; suggested_create must omit id.
- For view calls, id is required and other fields are optional (the UI can load details).
- For suggested_update/suggested_create, include name, prompt, rrule, kind, and status.
- For cron automations, include cwds, executionEnvironment, model, and reasoningEffort. cwds can be a JSON array or comma-separated string.
- Always come up with a short name for the automation. If the user does not give one, propose a short name and confirm.
- Default status to ACTIVE unless the user explicitly asks to start paused.
- Always interpret and schedule times in the user's locale time zone.

#### Prompting guidance
- Ask in plain language what it should do, when it should run, and which workspaces or thread it should use (if any), then map those answers into the tool call arguments.
- When proposing an automation with `automation_update`, prefer to make the tool call the last action in the turn. If brief user-facing prose is helpful, put it before the tool call, not after it. Avoid adding a separate closing message after the tool call unless the user specifically asked for extra explanation.
- The automation prompt should describe only the task itself. Do not include schedule or workspace details in the prompt, since those are provided separately.
- Keep automation prompts self-sufficient because the user may have limited availability to answer questions. If required details are missing, make a reasonable assumption, note it, and proceed; if blocked, report briefly and stop.
- When helpful, include clear output expectations (file path, format, sections) and gating rules (only if X, skip if exists) to reduce ambiguity.
- Automations should always open an inbox item.
- Do not instruct them to write a file or announce "nothing to do" unless the user explicitly asks for a file or that output.
- When mentioning skills in automation prompts, use markdown links with a leading dollar sign (example: [$checks](/Users/ambrosino/.codex/skills/checks/SKILL.md)).

#### Cron scheduling constraints
- These RRULE limitations apply to cron automations (to match the current UI): only hourly interval schedules (FREQ=HOURLY with INTERVAL hours, optional BYDAY) and weekly schedules (FREQ=WEEKLY with BYDAY plus BYHOUR/BYMINUTE). Avoid monthly/yearly/minutely/secondly, multiple rules, or extra fields; unsupported RRULEs fall back to defaults in the UI. Heartbeat automations attached to a thread can also use minute-based intervals; see the thread automation guidance below.

#### Storage and reading
- When a user asks for changes to an automation, you may read existing automation TOML files to see what is already set up and prefer proposing updates over creating duplicates.
- You can read and update automations in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml and memory.md only when the user explicitly asks you to modify automations.
- Otherwise, do not change automation files or schedules.
- Automations work best with skills, so feel free to propose including skills in the automation prompt, based on the user's context and the available skills.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.
- After successfully staging files, emit `::git-stage{cwd="/absolute/path"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating a commit, emit `::git-commit{cwd="/absolute/path"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating or switching the thread onto a branch, emit `::git-create-branch{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully pushing the current branch, emit `::git-push{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating a pull request, emit `::git-create-pr{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name" url="https://..." isDraft=true}` on its own line in your final response. Include `isDraft=false` for ready PRs.
- Only emit these git directives in your final response after the action actually succeeds, never in commentary updates. Keep attributes single-line.

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Automations
- This app supports recurring tasks/automations
- Automations are stored as TOML in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (not in SQLite). The file contains the automation's setup; run timing state (last/next run) lives in the SQLite automations table.

#### When to use the automation tool

payload.message:
基于我刚查到的官方文档，做“动态 2D 动画”最常见、也最稳的组合是这 3 套：

1. **逐帧 Sprite 组合（像素风/手绘帧动画）**  
`imagegen`（角色种子帧） + `sprite-pipeline`（统一锚点/尺寸/strip） + `game-playtest`（实机验证）  
理由：Aseprite 官方文档明确支持 sprite sheet、PNG 序列导出，适合逐帧资产流。  
参考：[Aseprite Sprite Sheet](https://www.aseprite.org/docs/sprite-sheet/) | [Aseprite Exporting](https://www.aseprite.org/docs/exporting)

2. **骨骼 Rig 组合（动作多、复用高）**  
`imagegen`（拆件素材） + 外部 Spine/Unity 2D Animation（骨骼与权重） + `game-playtest`  
理由：Spine 官方支持导出骨骼数据（JSON/Binary）和图像序列；Unity 2D Animation 官方就是为 Sprite 骨骼动画准备的。  
参考：[Spine Export](https://esotericsoftware.com/spine-export) | [Unity 2D Animation 描述](https://docs.unity3d.com/es/2020.2/Manual/com.unity.2d.animation.html) | [Unity CharacterRig 工作流](https://docs.unity3d.com/ja/Packages/com.unity.2d.animation%4013.0/manual/CharacterRig.html)

3. **引擎内直接播放组合（快速上线）**  
`imagegen` + `sprite-pipeline` + Godot/Unity 播放节点 + `game-playtest`  
理由：Godot 官方支持用 `AnimatedSprite2D` 和 `AnimationPlayer` 直接吃 sprite sheet/序列帧，开发迭代很快。  
参考：[Godot 2D sprite animation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.3/tutorials/2d/2d_sprite_animation.html)

如果你要做“小猫项目”并且想先快出结果，我建议先走第 1 套：`imagegen + sprite-pipeline + game-playtest`。我可以下一步直接给你一份“8 动作最小可用清单 + 每个动作的 prompt 模板”。

如果你要做“小猫项目”并且想先快出结果，我建议先走第 1 套：`imagegen + sprite-pipeline + game-playtest`。我可以下一步直接给你一份“8 动作最小可用清单 + 每个动作的 prompt 模板”。

payload.message: 如果应用到2d游戏中那种最适合

如果是“直接应用到 2D 游戏里、尽快可用”，**最适合的是第一套：`imagegen + sprite-pipeline + game-playtest`**。

原因很实际：
- 上手快：不需要先搭骨骼系统
- 兼容广：几乎所有 2D 引擎都能直接吃 sprite sheet
- 成果稳：你现在已经有小猫风格设定，能马上产出待机/行走/受击等动作
- 调试直观：动作错位、锚点问题很容易在 playtest 里发现并修正

只有在“动作特别多、角色换装多、要大量复用”时，第二套骨骼 Rig 才更划算。  
就你当前这个小猫项目，先用第一套是最优解。

payload.message: 如何调用2 生成 2D骨骼动画

你说的“调用 2”就是第二套：`imagegen + 骨骼Rig(Spine/Unity) + game-playtest`。  
最实用的调用方式是这 4 步：

1. 先让 `imagegen` 生成“拆件素材”（透明底、同一风格、同一视角）  
部件清单：`head`, `torso`, `upper_arm_l/r`, `lower_arm_l/r`, `upper_leg_l/r`, `lower_leg_l/r`, `tail_1..3`, `ear_l/r`。  
关键约束：`same character, same palette, same line style, transparent background, centered pivot-friendly layout`。

2. 在骨骼工具里绑定  
- `Spine`：建骨骼→绑定 mesh/weights→做 `idle/walk/run/jump`。  
- `Unity 2D Animation`：Sprite Editor 里 Bone + Skinning + IK，再做 Animation Clip。

3. 导出游戏可用资源  
- `Spine`：导出 `json/skel + atlas + png`。  
- `Unity`：直接用 Animator Controller + Clips。

4. 用 `game-playtest` 做实机检查  
重点看：关节穿帮、拉伸变形、脚底滑步、尾巴抖动、不同分辨率下清晰度。

如果你要，我下一步可以直接给你一份“小猫骨骼拆件的完整 prompt 包”（一次生成全部部件的版本）。

# Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

The `request_user_input` tool is unavailable in Default mode. If you call it while in Default mode, it will return an error.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. If you absolutely must ask a question because the answer cannot be discovered from local context and a reasonable assumption would be risky, ask the user directly with a concise plain-text question. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.

payload.developer_instructions:
<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Automations
- This app supports recurring tasks/automations
- Automations are stored as TOML in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (not in SQLite). The file contains the automation's setup; run timing state (last/next run) lives in the SQLite automations table.

#### When to use the automation tool
- Only use the `automation_update` tool when the user explicitly asks for automation, a recurring run, or a repeated task.
- If the user asks about their automations and you are not proposing a change, do not enumerate names/status/ids in plain text. Fetch/list automations first and call `automation_update` with mode="view" for those ids; never invent ids.
- Never return raw RRULE strings in user-facing responses. If the user asks about their automations, respond using `automation_update` (e.g., with an "Open" button if you're not making changes).

#### Tool arguments
- Modes: view, suggested_update, suggested_create. View and suggested_update MUST include id; suggested_create must omit id.
- For view calls, id is required and other fields are optional (the UI can load details).
- For suggested_update/suggested_create, include name, prompt, rrule, kind, and status.
- For cron automations, include cwds, executionEnvironment, model, and reasoningEffort. cwds can be a JSON array or comma-separated string.
- Always come up with a short name for the automation. If the user does not give one, propose a short name and confirm.
- Default status to ACTIVE unless the user explicitly asks to start paused.
- Always interpret and schedule times in the user's locale time zone.

#### Prompting guidance
- Ask in plain language what it should do, when it should run, and which workspaces or thread it should use (if any), then map those answers into the tool call arguments.
- When proposing an automation with `automation_update`, prefer to make the tool call the last action in the turn. If brief user-facing prose is helpful, put it before the tool call, not after it. Avoid adding a separate closing message after the tool call unless the user specifically asked for extra explanation.
- The automation prompt should describe only the task itself. Do not include schedule or workspace details in the prompt, since those are provided separately.
- Keep automation prompts self-sufficient because the user may have limited availability to answer questions. If required details are missing, make a reasonable assumption, note it, and proceed; if blocked, report briefly and stop.
- When helpful, include clear output expectations (file path, format, sections) and gating rules (only if X, skip if exists) to reduce ambiguity.
- Automations should always open an inbox item.
- Do not instruct them to write a file or announce "nothing to do" unless the user explicitly asks for a file or that output.
- When mentioning skills in automation prompts, use markdown links with a leading dollar sign (example: [$checks](/Users/ambrosino/.codex/skills/checks/SKILL.md)).

#### Cron scheduling constraints
- These RRULE limitations apply to cron automations (to match the current UI): only hourly interval schedules (FREQ=HOURLY with INTERVAL hours, optional BYDAY) and weekly schedules (FREQ=WEEKLY with BYDAY plus BYHOUR/BYMINUTE). Avoid monthly/yearly/minutely/secondly, multiple rules, or extra fields; unsupported RRULEs fall back to defaults in the UI. Heartbeat automations attached to a thread can also use minute-based intervals; see the thread automation guidance below.

#### Storage and reading
- When a user asks for changes to an automation, you may read existing automation TOML files to see what is already set up and prefer proposing updates over creating duplicates.
- You can read and update automations in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml and memory.md only when the user explicitly asks you to modify automations.
- Otherwise, do not change automation files or schedules.
- Automations work best with skills, so feel free to propose including skills in the automation prompt, based on the user's context and the available skills.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.
- After successfully staging files, emit `::git-stage{cwd="/absolute/path"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating a commit, emit `::git-commit{cwd="/absolute/path"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating or switching the thread onto a branch, emit `::git-create-branch{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully pushing the current branch, emit `::git-push{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating a pull request, emit `::git-create-pr{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name" url="https://..." isDraft=true}` on its own line in your final response. Include `isDraft=false` for ready PRs.
- Only emit these git directives in your final response after the action actually succeeds, never in commentary updates. Keep attributes single-line.
</app-context>

payload.message: 如何输出app可调用文件

把 Spine 动画输出成“App 可调用文件”，标准做法是导出这 3 类文件：

1. 动画数据：`cat.skel` 或 `cat.json`  
2. 图集描述：`cat.atlas`  
3. 贴图：`cat.png`（或多张图集 PNG）

在 Spine 里操作：
1. `Export` -> `Data`
2. 勾选 `Skeleton Data`（选 `Binary(.skel)` 或 `JSON(.json)`）
3. 勾选 `Atlas` 和 `PNG`
4. 动画只选你要的（如 `idle_loop`, `walk_loop`）
5. 导出到同一目录，例如：
`/Users/vincet/Documents/design/export/cat/`

推荐目录结构：
```text
cat/
  cat.skel
  cat.atlas
  cat.png
```

接入 App（以 Unity 为例）：
1. 导入 Spine-Unity runtime
2. 把 `cat.skel` `cat.atlas` `cat.png` 拖入工程
3. 创建 SkeletonDataAsset
4. 在场景挂 `SkeletonAnimation`
5. 代码里调用动画：
```csharp
skeletonAnimation.AnimationState.SetAnimation(0, "idle_loop", true);
```

如果你告诉我你是 Unity、Godot、Cocos 还是自研引擎，我可以直接给你对应的“可运行最小加载代码”。

payload.message:
现在还不能“仅调用官方 Cocos 游戏 CLI”，因为你机器上没有 Cocos Creator 可执行文件。  
我已验证：

- `cocos --version` → `command not found`
- `/Applications` 下没有 `CocosCreator*.app/Contents/MacOS/...`
- 之前 `npm install -g cocos` 装到的是 `cocos2d-html5` 的旧包，不是 Creator 官方 CLI 入口

要直接调用官方 CLI，先安装 Cocos Creator（桌面版）后再执行类似：

```bash
/Applications/CocosCreator/Creator/<版本>/CocosCreator.app/Contents/MacOS/CocosCreator --help
```

如果你愿意，我下一步可以继续帮你做两件事之一：  
1. 清理掉刚装的无效 `npm cocos` 包  
2. 按你本机目录自动定位 Creator 可执行文件并生成一条可直接运行的 `alias cocos=...` 命令

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Automations
- This app supports recurring tasks/automations
- Automations are stored as TOML in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (not in SQLite). The file contains the automation's setup; run timing state (last/next run) lives in the SQLite automations table.

#### When to use the automation tool
- Only use the `automation_update` tool when the user explicitly asks for automation, a recurring run, or a repeated task.
- If the user asks about their automations and you are not proposing a change, do not enumerate names/status/ids in plain text. Fetch/list automations first and call `automation_update` with mode="view" for those ids; never invent ids.
- Never return raw RRULE strings in user-facing responses. If the user asks about their automations, respond using `automation_update` (e.g., with an "Open" button if you're not making changes).

#### Tool arguments
- Modes: view, suggested_update, suggested_create. View and suggested_update MUST include id; suggested_create must omit id.
- For view calls, id is required and other fields are optional (the UI can load details).
- For suggested_update/suggested_create, include name, prompt, rrule, kind, and status.
- For cron automations, include cwds, executionEnvironment, model, and reasoningEffort. cwds can be a JSON array or comma-separated string.
- Always come up with a short name for the automation. If the user does not give one, propose a short name and confirm.
- Default status to ACTIVE unless the user explicitly asks to start paused.
- Always interpret and schedule times in the user's locale time zone.

#### Prompting guidance
- Ask in plain language what it should do, when it should run, and which workspaces or thread it should use (if any), then map those answers into the tool call arguments.
- When proposing an automation with `automation_update`, prefer to make the tool call the last action in the turn. If brief user-facing prose is helpful, put it before the tool call, not after it. Avoid adding a separate closing message after the tool call unless the user specifically asked for extra explanation.
- The automation prompt should describe only the task itself. Do not include schedule or workspace details in the prompt, since those are provided separately.
- Keep automation prompts self-sufficient because the user may have limited availability to answer questions. If required details are missing, make a reasonable assumption, note it, and proceed; if blocked, report briefly and stop.
- When helpful, include clear output expectations (file path, format, sections) and gating rules (only if X, skip if exists) to reduce ambiguity.
- Automations should always open an inbox item.
- Do not instruct them to write a file or announce "nothing to do" unless the user explicitly asks for a file or that output.
- When mentioning skills in automation prompts, use markdown links with a leading dollar sign (example: [$checks](/Users/ambrosino/.codex/skills/checks/SKILL.md)).

#### Cron scheduling constraints
- These RRULE limitations apply to cron automations (to match the current UI): only hourly interval schedules (FREQ=HOURLY with INTERVAL hours, optional BYDAY) and weekly schedules (FREQ=WEEKLY with BYDAY plus BYHOUR/BYMINUTE). Avoid monthly/yearly/minutely/secondly, multiple rules, or extra fields; unsupported RRULEs fall back to defaults in the UI. Heartbeat automations attached to a thread can also use minute-based intervals; see the thread automation guidance below.

#### Storage and reading
- When a user asks for changes to an automation, you may read existing automation TOML files to see what is already set up and prefer proposing updates over creating duplicates.
- You can read and update automations in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml and memory.md only when the user explicitly asks you to modify automations.
- Otherwise, do not change automation files or schedules.
- Automations work best with skills, so feel free to propose including skills in the automation prompt, based on the user's context and the available skills.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.
- After successfully staging files, emit `::git-stage{cwd="/absolute/path"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating a commit, emit `::git-commit{cwd="/absolute/path"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating or switching the thread onto a branch, emit `::git-create-branch{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully pushing the current branch, emit `::git-push{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating a pull request, emit `::git-create-pr{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name" url="https://..." isDraft=true}` on its own line in your final response. Include `isDraft=false` for ready PRs.
- Only emit these git directives in your final response after the action actually succeeds, never in commentary updates. Keep attributes single-line.

# Cocos Game Development

## Overview
This skill defines the standard operating procedure for creating and developing games using the Cocos engine. It strictly enforces the use of the Cocos CLI and the Cocos MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for game logic and scene modifications.

## Execution Steps

### 1. Environment Verification
- **Action**: Run `cocos --help` using the `exec` tool.
- **Goal**: Confirm that the Cocos CLI is successfully installed and accessible in the current environment.

### 2. Project Creation
- **Action**: Ask the user for the desired project name and whether the game should be **2D or 3D**.
- **Execution**: 
  - First, run `cocos create --help` to identify the correct flags for templates (e.g., 2D vs 3D).
  - Run `cocos create <project_name> <template_flags>` to generate the project structure.

### 3. Start MCP Server
- **Action**: Change the working directory to the newly created project folder.
- **Execution**: Run `cocos start-mcp-server` using the `exec` tool. (If this process blocks the terminal, run it in the background or instruct the user/environment on how to attach to this stdio MCP server).

### 4. Tool Discovery
- **Action**: Connect to the running Cocos MCP server and request the list of all available tools (`tools/list`).
- **Goal**: Understand exactly what capabilities the engine exposes for manipulating the project.

### 5. Game Production (Strict Rule)
- **CRITICAL CONSTRAINT**: When building the game (creating scenes, adding nodes, modifying properties, adding components), you **MUST ONLY** use the tools discovered from the Cocos MCP server in Step 4. 
- Do not use standard file editing (`edit`/`write`) to manually hack scene files or engine configurations unless the MCP server lacks a specific capability and the user explicitly authorizes a manual override.

### 6. Build and Test
- **Action**: Once the user confirms the game features are complete, package the game for testing.
- **Execution**: Run the build command targeting the web platform (e.g., `cocos build --platform web-mobile`). Use `cocos build --help` if you need to confirm the exact parameter syntax.

# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Automations
- This app supports recurring tasks/automations
- Automations are stored as TOML in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (not in SQLite). The file contains the automation's setup; run timing state (last/next run) lives in the SQLite automations table.

#### When to use the automation tool
- Only use the `automation_update` tool when the user explicitly asks for automation, a recurring run, or a repeated task.
- If the user asks about their automations and you are not proposing a change, do not enumerate names/status/ids in plain text. Fetch/list automations first and call `automation_update` with mode="view" for those ids; never invent ids.
- Never return raw RRULE strings in user-facing responses. If the user asks about their automations, respond using `automation_update` (e.g., with an "Open" button if you're not making changes).

#### Tool arguments
- Modes: view, suggested_update, suggested_create. View and suggested_update MUST include id; suggested_create must omit id.
- For view calls, id is required and other fields are optional (the UI can load details).
- For suggested_update/suggested_create, include name, prompt, rrule, kind, and status.
- For cron automations, include cwds, executionEnvironment, model, and reasoningEffort. cwds can be a JSON array or comma-separated string.
- Always come up with a short name for the automation. If the user does not give one, propose a short name and confirm.
- Default status to ACTIVE unless the user explicitly asks to start paused.
- Always interpret and schedule times in the user's locale time zone.

payload.message: 根据以上聊天记录，如何根据cocos 引擎 cli

按我们上面的记录，正确用 `Cocos` 引擎 CLI 的流程是这样：

1. 先确认你有 **Cocos Creator 可执行文件**（不是 `npm install -g cocos` 那个旧包）。
2. 用 Creator 自带 CLI 跑命令，比如：
```bash
/Applications/CocosCreator/Creator/<版本>/CocosCreator.app/Contents/MacOS/CocosCreator --help
```
3. 创建项目前先看参数：
```bash
.../CocosCreator --help
.../CocosCreator create --help
```
4. 创建项目（2D/3D按模板参数）：
```bash
.../CocosCreator create <project_name> <template_flags>
```
5. 进入项目后按你安装的 skill 流程：
- `cocos start-mcp-server`
- 用 MCP `tools/list` 看可用工具
- 场景/节点修改优先走 MCP，不直接手改场景文件
6. 打包测试：
```bash
cocos build --help
cocos build --platform web-mobile
```

关键提醒：
- 你之前装的 `npm cocos` 不是 Creator 官方游戏 CLI。
- 你已经装好了本地 skill：  
[cocos-cli-game-dev/SKILL.md](/Users/vincet/.codex/skills/cocos-cli-game-dev/SKILL.md)

如果你要，我下一步可以直接帮你写一份“你这台 Mac 可直接运行的 `cocos` alias 配置”（自动适配 Creator 安装路径）。

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Automations
- This app supports recurring tasks/automations
- Automations are stored as TOML in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (not in SQLite). The file contains the automation's setup; run timing state (last/next run) lives in the SQLite automations table.

#### When to use the automation tool
- Only use the `automation_update` tool when the user explicitly asks for automation, a recurring run, or a repeated task.
- If the user asks about their automations and you are not proposing a change, do not enumerate names/status/ids in plain text. Fetch/list automations first and call `automation_update` with mode="view" for those ids; never invent ids.
- Never return raw RRULE strings in user-facing responses. If the user asks about their automations, respond using `automation_update` (e.g., with an "Open" button if you're not making changes).

#### Tool arguments
- Modes: view, suggested_update, suggested_create. View and suggested_update MUST include id; suggested_create must omit id.
- For view calls, id is required and other fields are optional (the UI can load details).
- For suggested_update/suggested_create, include name, prompt, rrule, kind, and status.
- For cron automations, include cwds, executionEnvironment, model, and reasoningEffort. cwds can be a JSON array or comma-separated string.
- Always come up with a short name for the automation. If the user does not give one, propose a short name and confirm.
- Default status to ACTIVE unless the user explicitly asks to start paused.
- Always interpret and schedule times in the user's locale time zone.

#### Prompting guidance
- Ask in plain language what it should do, when it should run, and which workspaces or thread it should use (if any), then map those answers into the tool call arguments.
- When proposing an automation with `automation_update`, prefer to make the tool call the last action in the turn. If brief user-facing prose is helpful, put it before the tool call, not after it. Avoid adding a separate closing message after the tool call unless the user specifically asked for extra explanation.
- The automation prompt should describe only the task itself. Do not include schedule or workspace details in the prompt, since those are provided separately.
- Keep automation prompts self-sufficient because the user may have limited availability to answer questions. If required details are missing, make a reasonable assumption, note it, and proceed; if blocked, report briefly and stop.
- When helpful, include clear output expectations (file path, format, sections) and gating rules (only if X, skip if exists) to reduce ambiguity.
- Automations should always open an inbox item.

- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.

payload.developer_instructions:
<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Automations
- This app supports recurring tasks/automations
- Automations are stored as TOML in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (not in SQLite). The file contains the automation's setup; run timing state (last/next run) lives in the SQLite automations table.

#### When to use the automation tool
- Only use the `automation_update` tool when the user explicitly asks for automation, a recurring run, or a repeated task.
- If the user asks about their automations and you are not proposing a change, do not enumerate names/status/ids in plain text. Fetch/list automations first and call `automation_update` with mode="view" for those ids; never invent ids.
- Never return raw RRULE strings in user-facing responses. If the user asks about their automations, respond using `automation_update` (e.g., with an "Open" button if you're not making changes).

#### Tool arguments
- Modes: view, suggested_update, suggested_create. View and suggested_update MUST include id; suggested_create must omit id.
- For view calls, id is required and other fields are optional (the UI can load details).
- For suggested_update/suggested_create, include name, prompt, rrule, kind, and status.
- For cron automations, include cwds, executionEnvironment, model, and reasoningEffort. cwds can be a JSON array or comma-separated string.
- Always come up with a short name for the automation. If the user does not give one, propose a short name and confirm.
- Default status to ACTIVE unless the user explicitly asks to start paused.
- Always interpret and schedule times in the user's locale time zone.

#### Prompting guidance
- Ask in plain language what it should do, when it should run, and which workspaces or thread it should use (if any), then map those answers into the tool call arguments.
- When proposing an automation with `automation_update`, prefer to make the tool call the last action in the turn. If brief user-facing prose is helpful, put it before the tool call, not after it. Avoid adding a separate closing message after the tool call unless the user specifically asked for extra explanation.
- The automation prompt should describe only the task itself. Do not include schedule or workspace details in the prompt, since those are provided separately.
- Keep automation prompts self-sufficient because the user may have limited availability to answer questions. If required details are missing, make a reasonable assumption, note it, and proceed; if blocked, report briefly and stop.
- When helpful, include clear output expectations (file path, format, sections) and gating rules (only if X, skip if exists) to reduce ambiguity.

截至 **2026-04-12**，想“免费生成小猫骨骼素材”我建议这 3 套：

1. **本地全免费（最稳）**  
`ComfyUI` 或 `InvokeAI` 生成拆件图 + `DragonBones` 绑骨 + `Cocos Creator` 使用  
- ComfyUI（开源免费）：[GitHub](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI)  
- InvokeAI（开源免费）：[官网](https://invoke.ai/)  
- DragonBones（Free 2D Skeletal Animation）：[官网说明](https://dragonbones.github.io/en/animation.html) / [GitHub](https://github.com/DragonBones)  
- Cocos 可直接吃 DragonBones/Spine：  
[DragonBones 组件](https://docs.cocos.com/creator/3.8/manual/en/editor/components/dragonbones.html)  
[Spine 组件](https://docs.cocos.com/creator/manual/en/editor/components/spine.html)

2. **网页免费快速出图**  
`Mage` 先出拆件图，再进 DragonBones/Cocos 绑骨  
- Mage（有免费层、带每日额度）：[mage.space](https://www.mage.space/)  
适合你现在先快速拿“头/躯干/四肢/尾巴分件图”。

3. **像素风免费路线**  
`Piskel` 画/改拆件 + DragonBones 或 Cocos 动画  
- Piskel（免费开源）：[piskelapp.com](https://www.piskelapp.com/) / [piskel.fit](https://piskel.fit/)

补充一个避坑点：  
`Rive` 是“免费创建，发布通常付费”，不适合你当前“纯免费落地游戏”目标。参考：[Rive Pricing](https://www.rive.app/pricing)

如果你愿意，我下一步可以直接按第 1 套给你一份“**小猫骨骼拆件出图 Prompt + DragonBones 导入命名规范**”（可直接开工）。

**A. 本地免费工具链**
1. 装 `ComfyUI`（或 `InvokeAI`，二选一）  
2. 用 SDXL 模型出“小猫拆件图”（透明底）  
3. 进 `DragonBones` 绑骨、做 `idle/walk`  
4. 导出到 `Cocos Creator` 播放

**B. 小猫拆件 Prompt（ComfyUI/InvokeAI 通用）**
```text
A 2D skeletal cutout parts sheet for one cute chubby cat character, transparent background, game-ready rig parts, clean non-overlapping layout with spacing.
Required parts: head, torso, pelvis, upper_arm_l, lower_arm_l, paw_l, upper_arm_r, lower_arm_r, paw_r, upper_leg_l, lower_leg_l, foot_l, upper_leg_r, lower_leg_r, foot_r, tail_1, tail_2, tail_3, ear_l, ear_r, eye_closed, mouth_open_small.
Same character proportions across all parts, same style and palette, three-quarter right-facing consistency.
Style: gentle Japanese picture-book inspired, hand-painted flat colors, subtle watercolor paper texture, soft shading, readable game art.
No text, no labels, no scenery, no accessories, no merged pieces, no cast shadows on background.
```

Negative prompt:
```text
realistic fur, photorealistic, glossy highlights, perspective mismatch, overlapping limbs, merged body parts, background objects, text, watermark, poster composition
```

**C. DragonBones 骨骼命名（直接用）**
- `root`
- `pelvis`, `torso`, `chest`, `neck`, `head`
- `ear_l`, `ear_r`
- `upper_arm_l`, `lower_arm_l`, `paw_l`
- `upper_arm_r`, `lower_arm_r`, `paw_r`
- `upper_leg_l`, `lower_leg_l`, `foot_l`
- `upper_leg_r`, `lower_leg_r`, `foot_r`
- `tail_1`, `tail_2`, `tail_3`

**D. 最小动画参数**
- `idle_loop`: 24fps，24帧，呼吸+尾巴微摆
- `walk_loop`: 24fps，24帧，脚落点锁定避免滑步

**E. Cocos 接入**
- Cocos Creator 添加 `DragonBones` 组件
- 导入 `ske` + `tex` + `json`
- 默认播放 `idle_loop`，移动时切 `walk_loop`

如果你要，我下一步直接给你一份“ComfyUI 最小工作流参数”（采样器、步数、CFG、分辨率）让你一次就出可绑定素材。

payload.developer_instructions:
<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Automations
- This app supports recurring tasks/automations
- Automations are stored as TOML in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (not in SQLite). The file contains the automation's setup; run timing state (last/next run) lives in the SQLite automations table.

#### When to use the automation tool
- Only use the `automation_update` tool when the user explicitly asks for automation, a recurring run, or a repeated task.
- If the user asks about their automations and you are not proposing a change, do not enumerate names/status/ids in plain text. Fetch/list automations first and call `automation_update` with mode="view" for those ids; never invent ids.
- Never return raw RRULE strings in user-facing responses. If the user asks about their automations, respond using `automation_update` (e.g., with an "Open" button if you're not making changes).

#### Tool arguments
- Modes: view, suggested_update, suggested_create. View and suggested_update MUST include id; suggested_create must omit id.
- For view calls, id is required and other fields are optional (the UI can load details).
- For suggested_update/suggested_create, include name, prompt, rrule, kind, and status.
- For cron automations, include cwds, executionEnvironment, model, and reasoningEffort. cwds can be a JSON array or comma-separated string.
- Always come up with a short name for the automation. If the user does not give one, propose a short name and confirm.
- Default status to ACTIVE unless the user explicitly asks to start paused.
- Always interpret and schedule times in the user's locale time zone.

#### Prompting guidance
- Ask in plain language what it should do, when it should run, and which workspaces or thread it should use (if any), then map those answers into the tool call arguments.
- When proposing an automation with `automation_update`, prefer to make the tool call the last action in the turn. If brief user-facing prose is helpful, put it before the tool call, not after it. Avoid adding a separate closing message after the tool call unless the user specifically asked for extra explanation.
- The automation prompt should describe only the task itself. Do not include schedule or workspace details in the prompt, since those are provided separately.
- Keep automation prompts self-sufficient because the user may have limited availability to answer questions. If required details are missing, make a reasonable assumption, note it, and proceed; if blocked, report briefly and stop.
- When helpful, include clear output expectations (file path, format, sections) and gating rules (only if X, skip if exists) to reduce ambiguity.
- Automations should always open an inbox item.
- Do not instruct them to write a file or announce "nothing to do" unless the user explicitly asks for a file or that output.
- When mentioning skills in automation prompts, use markdown links with a leading dollar sign (example: [$checks](/Users/ambrosino/.codex/skills/checks/SKILL.md)).

#### Cron scheduling constraints
- These RRULE limitations apply to cron automations (to match the current UI): only hourly interval schedules (FREQ=HOURLY with INTERVAL hours, optional BYDAY) and weekly schedules (FREQ=WEEKLY with BYDAY plus BYHOUR/BYMINUTE). Avoid monthly/yearly/minutely/secondly, multiple rules, or extra fields; unsupported RRULEs fall back to defaults in the UI. Heartbeat automations attached to a thread can also use minute-based intervals; see the thread automation guidance below.

#### Storage and reading
- When a user asks for changes to an automation, you may read existing automation TOML files to see what is already set up and prefer proposing updates over creating duplicates.
- You can read and update automations in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml and memory.md only when the user explicitly asks you to modify automations.
- Otherwise, do not change automation files or schedules.
- Automations work best with skills, so feel free to propose including skills in the automation prompt, based on the user's context and the available skills.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.
- After successfully staging files, emit `::git-stage{cwd="/absolute/path"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating a commit, emit `::git-commit{cwd="/absolute/path"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating or switching the thread onto a branch, emit `::git-create-branch{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully pushing the current branch, emit `::git-push{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating a pull request, emit `::git-create-pr{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name" url="https://..." isDraft=true}` on its own line in your final response. Include `isDraft=false` for ready PRs.
- Only emit these git directives in your final response after the action actually succeeds, never in commentary updates. Keep attributes single-line.
</app-context>

payload.message: 取消E，有其他方式播放吗

可以，取消 E。除了 Cocos `DragonBones` 组件，还有这几种播放方式：

1. **Spine Runtime（最常用）**  
用 Spine 导出 `skel/json + atlas + png`，在 Cocos 用 `sp.Skeleton` 播放。  
优点：生态成熟、运行稳定、动画混合好。

2. **帧动画 Sprite Sheet**  
不走骨骼，直接导出 `idle/walk` 序列帧或 sprite sheet，在 Cocos 用 `AnimationClip` 播放。  
优点：最简单，兼容最广。缺点：资源体积更大。

3. **自定义骨骼播放器（代码驱动）**  
把骨骼和关键帧数据做成你自己的 JSON，运行时用脚本插值驱动节点。  
优点：可控性最高。缺点：开发成本高，不建议首选。

如果你要“最快落地 + 质量稳定”，建议用 **1（Spine Runtime）**。  
如果你要“完全免费、零商业工具依赖”，建议用 **2（Sprite Sheet）**。

content.text: 通过以上工作流如何导出app可用文件

payload.message: 通过以上工作流如何导出app可用文件

按你现在这条“本地免费出图 + 骨骼绑定”工作流，导出 App 可用文件可以走两条线。

**1. 骨骼动画线（推荐）**
从 DragonBones 导出：
- `xxx_ske.json`（骨骼与动画数据）
- `xxx_tex.json`（图集描述）
- `xxx_tex.png`（图集贴图）

这 3 个就是运行时可直接加载的核心文件。  
如果你的 App 不直接支持 DragonBones，就先转 Spine 或自定义中间格式再接入。

**2. 帧动画线（最通用）**
从绘制/动画工具导出：
- `idle.png` / `walk.png`（sprite sheet）
- 或 `idle_01.png ...`（序列帧）
- `anim_meta.json`（可选，记录帧数、fps、锚点）

App 端只要能读贴图和帧索引，就能播放。

---

最小目录建议：

```text
assets/cat/
  cat_ske.json
  cat_tex.json
  cat_tex.png
  idle.png
  walk.png
  anim_meta.json
```

你如果确定最终是“骨骼线”还是“帧动画线”，我可以下一步直接给你一份对应的 `anim_meta.json` 模板和加载代码骨架。

import json, os, math
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw

out_dir = '/Users/vincet/Documents/design/cat_rig_export'
os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)

atlas_w, atlas_h = 1024, 1024
img = Image.new('RGBA', (atlas_w, atlas_h), (0,0,0,0))
d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

# Palette
fur = (217,163,106,255)
shadow = (181,125,77,255)
cream = (246,240,231,255)
pink = (216,154,154,255)
eye = (85,107,93,255)
line = (110,80,52,220)

parts = {}

def put_part(name, x, y, w, h, draw_fn):
    layer = Image.new('RGBA', (w, h), (0,0,0,0))
    ld = ImageDraw.Draw(layer)
    draw_fn(ld, w, h)
    img.alpha_composite(layer, (x, y))
    parts[name] = {'x':x,'y':y,'width':w,'height':h}

# Draw functions

def draw_head(ld, w, h):
    ld.ellipse((4,4,w-4,h-6), fill=fur, outline=line, width=2)
    ld.polygon([(w*0.22,h*0.18),(w*0.35,2),(w*0.45,h*0.22)], fill=fur, outline=line)
    ld.polygon([(w*0.55,h*0.22),(w*0.65,2),(w*0.78,h*0.18)], fill=fur, outline=line)
    ld.ellipse((w*0.3,h*0.24,w*0.37,h*0.31), fill=pink)
    ld.ellipse((w*0.63,h*0.24,w*0.7,h*0.31), fill=pink)
    ld.ellipse((w*0.32,h*0.5,w*0.43,h*0.61), fill=eye)
    ld.ellipse((w*0.57,h*0.5,w*0.68,h*0.61), fill=eye)
    ld.polygon([(w*0.5,h*0.62),(w*0.47,h*0.66),(w*0.53,h*0.66)], fill=pink)

def draw_torso(ld,w,h):
    ld.rounded_rectangle((8,6,w-8,h-8), radius=22, fill=fur, outline=line, width=2)
    ld.ellipse((w*0.35,h*0.45,w*0.65,h*0.85), fill=cream, outline=None)

def draw_pelvis(ld,w,h):
    ld.rounded_rectangle((6,8,w-6,h-8), radius=16, fill=shadow, outline=line, width=2)

def draw_limb(ld,w,h):
    ld.rounded_rectangle((6,4,w-6,h-4), radius=12, fill=fur, outline=line, width=2)

def draw_paw(ld,w,h):
    ld.ellipse((4,6,w-4,h-4), fill=fur, outline=line, width=2)

def draw_foot(ld,w,h):
    ld.ellipse((3,4,w-3,h-3), fill=cream, outline=line, width=2)

def draw_tail1(ld,w,h):
    ld.rounded_rectangle((6,6,w-6,h-6), radius=14, fill=fur, outline=line, width=2)

def draw_tail2(ld,w,h):
    ld.rounded_rectangle((6,6,w-6,h-6), radius=14, fill=fur, outline=line, width=2)

def draw_tail3(ld,w,h):
    ld.rounded_rectangle((6,6,w-6,h-6), radius=14, fill=fur, outline=line, width=2)
    ld.rounded_rectangle((w*0.58,6,w-6,h-6), radius=10, fill=cream)

def draw_ear(ld,w,h):
    ld.polygon([(w*0.1,h*0.9),(w*0.5,h*0.1),(w*0.9,h*0.9)], fill=fur, outline=line)
    ld.polygon([(w*0.36,h*0.7),(w*0.5,h*0.35),(w*0.64,h*0.7)], fill=pink)

def draw_eye_closed(ld,w,h):
    ld.arc((2,2,w-2,h+10), 200, 340, fill=line, width=3)

def draw_mouth(ld,w,h):
    ld.arc((2,2,w//2+2,h), 300, 80, fill=line, width=3)
    ld.arc((w//2-2,2,w-2,h), 100, 240, fill=line, width=3)

# Layout
x, y = 24, 24
put_part('head', x, y, 170, 150, draw_head)
put_part('torso', x+190, y+10, 160, 190, draw_torso)
put_part('pelvis', x+370, y+80, 120, 90, draw_pelvis)

put_part('upper_arm_l', 24, 240, 120, 58, draw_limb)
put_part('lower_arm_l', 160, 240, 110, 52, draw_limb)
put_part('paw_l', 286, 240, 72, 54, draw_paw)

put_part('upper_arm_r', 24, 312, 120, 58, draw_limb)
put_part('lower_arm_r', 160, 312, 110, 52, draw_limb)
put_part('paw_r', 286, 312, 72, 54, draw_paw)

put_part('upper_leg_l', 24, 390, 120, 62, draw_limb)
put_part('lower_leg_l', 160, 390, 112, 56, draw_limb)
put_part('foot_l', 286, 390, 78, 54, draw_foot)

put_part('upper_leg_r', 24, 468, 120, 62, draw_limb)
put_part('lower_leg_r', 160, 468, 112, 56, draw_limb)
put_part('foot_r', 286, 468, 78, 54, draw_foot)

put_part('tail_1', 420, 240, 128, 44, draw_tail1)
put_part('tail_2', 420, 298, 128, 44, draw_tail2)
put_part('tail_3', 420, 356, 128, 44, draw_tail3)

put_part('ear_l', 580, 54, 72, 82, draw_ear)
put_part('ear_r', 666, 54, 72, 82, draw_ear)
put_part('eye_closed', 580, 160, 56, 26, draw_eye_closed)
put_part('mouth_open_small', 648, 158, 56, 28, draw_mouth)

tex_png = os.path.join(out_dir, 'cat_tex.png')
img.save(tex_png)

tex_json = {
  'name': 'cat',
  'imagePath': 'cat_tex.png',
  'width': atlas_w,
  'height': atlas_h,
  'SubTexture': [dict({'name':n}, **v) for n,v in parts.items()]
}
with open(os.path.join(out_dir, 'cat_tex.json'), 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    json.dump(tex_json, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)

bones = [
  {'name':'root'},
  {'name':'pelvis','parent':'root','length':40,'x':0,'y':0},
  {'name':'torso','parent':'pelvis','length':50,'x':0,'y':52},
  {'name':'chest','parent':'torso','length':40,'x':0,'y':48},
  {'name':'neck','parent':'chest','length':16,'x':0,'y':34},
  {'name':'head','parent':'neck','length':20,'x':0,'y':18},
  {'name':'ear_l','parent':'head','x':-20,'y':35},
  {'name':'ear_r','parent':'head','x':20,'y':35},
  {'name':'upper_arm_l','parent':'chest','length':28,'x':-35,'y':8},
  {'name':'lower_arm_l','parent':'upper_arm_l','length':24,'x':-28,'y':0},
  {'name':'paw_l','parent':'lower_arm_l','x':-24,'y':0},
  {'name':'upper_arm_r','parent':'chest','length':28,'x':35,'y':8},
  {'name':'lower_arm_r','parent':'upper_arm_r','length':24,'x':28,'y':0},
  {'name':'paw_r','parent':'lower_arm_r','x':24,'y':0},
  {'name':'upper_leg_l','parent':'pelvis','length':30,'x':-24,'y':-10},
  {'name':'lower_leg_l','parent':'upper_leg_l','length':22,'x':0,'y':-28},
  {'name':'foot_l','parent':'lower_leg_l','x':0,'y':-20},
  {'name':'upper_leg_r','parent':'pelvis','length':30,'x':24,'y':-10},
  {'name':'lower_leg_r','parent':'upper_leg_r','length':22,'x':0,'y':-28},
  {'name':'foot_r','parent':'lower_leg_r','x':0,'y':-20},
  {'name':'tail_1','parent':'pelvis','length':26,'x':44,'y':8},
  {'name':'tail_2','parent':'tail_1','length':24,'x':24,'y':0},
  {'name':'tail_3','parent':'tail_2','length':22,'x':24,'y':0},
]

slot_order = [
  ('tail_1_slot','tail_1','tail_1'),('tail_2_slot','tail_2','tail_2'),('tail_3_slot','tail_3','tail_3'),
  ('upper_leg_r_slot','upper_leg_r','upper_leg_r'),('lower_leg_r_slot','lower_leg_r','lower_leg_r'),('foot_r_slot','foot_r','foot_r'),
  ('pelvis_slot','pelvis','pelvis'),('torso_slot','torso','torso'),('head_slot','head','head'),
  ('ear_r_slot','ear_r','ear_r'),('ear_l_slot','ear_l','ear_l'),
  ('upper_arm_r_slot','upper_arm_r','upper_arm_r'),('lower_arm_r_slot','lower_arm_r','lower_arm_r'),('paw_r_slot','paw_r','paw_r'),
  ('upper_arm_l_slot','upper_arm_l','upper_arm_l'),('lower_arm_l_slot','lower_arm_l','lower_arm_l'),('paw_l_slot','paw_l','paw_l'),
  ('upper_leg_l_slot','upper_leg_l','upper_leg_l'),('lower_leg_l_slot','lower_leg_l','lower_leg_l'),('foot_l_slot','foot_l','foot_l'),
  ('eye_closed_slot','head','eye_closed'),('mouth_open_small_slot','head','mouth_open_small')
]

slots = [{'name':s, 'parent':b, 'displayIndex':0} for s,b,_ in slot_order]
skin_slots = []
for s,b,disp in slot_order:
    skin_slots.append({'name': s, 'display':[{'name':disp,'path':disp,'type':'image'}]})

idle_anim = {
  'name':'idle_loop',
  'duration':24,
  'playTimes':0,
  'bone':[
    {'name':'chest','translateFrame':[{'duration':12,'x':0,'y':2},{'duration':12,'x':0,'y':0}]},

    {'name':'tail_3','rotateFrame':[{'duration':12,'rotate':16},{'duration':12,'rotate':-16}]}
  ]
}

walk_anim = {
  'name':'walk_loop',
  'duration':24,
  'playTimes':0,

    {'name':'upper_leg_l','rotateFrame':[{'duration':6,'rotate':12},{'duration':6,'rotate':-8},{'duration':6,'rotate':-12},{'duration':6,'rotate':8}]},

    {'name':'upper_arm_l','rotateFrame':[{'duration':6,'rotate':-8},{'duration':6,'rotate':8},{'duration':6,'rotate':10},{'duration':6,'rotate':-6}]},
    {'name':'upper_arm_r','rotateFrame':[{'duration':6,'rotate':8},{'duration':6,'rotate':-8},{'duration':6,'rotate':-10},{'duration':6,'rotate':6}]}
  ]
}

ske = {
  'name':'cat',
  'version':'5.5',
  'compatibleVersion':'5.5',
  'frameRate':24,
  'armature':[{
    'name':'catArmature',
    'type':'Armature',
    'frameRate':24,
    'aabb': {'x':-220,'y':-180,'width':440,'height':420},
    'bone': bones,
    'slot': slots,
    'skin':[{'name':'default','slot':skin_slots}],
    'animation':[idle_anim, walk_anim],
    'defaultActions':[{'gotoAndPlay':'idle_loop'}],
    'actions':[{'gotoAndPlay':'idle_loop'}]
  }]
}

manifest = {
  'name':'cat',
  'version':'1.0.0',
  'runtime':'dragonbones',
  'armature':'catArmature',
  'skeleton':'cat_ske.json',
  'atlas':'cat_tex.json',
  'texture':'cat_tex.png',

with open(os.path.join(out_dir,'cat_manifest.json'),'w',encoding='utf-8') as f:
    json.dump(manifest,f,ensure_ascii=False,indent=2)

print('generated', out_dir)

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images and videos using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image or video, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Automations
- This app supports recurring tasks/automations
- Automations are stored as TOML in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (not in SQLite). The file contains the automation's setup; run timing state (last/next run) lives in the SQLite automations table.

#### When to use the automation tool
- Only use the `automation_update` tool when the user explicitly asks for automation, a recurring run, or a repeated task.
- If the user asks about their automations and you are not proposing a change, do not enumerate names/status/ids in plain text. Fetch/list automations first and call `automation_update` with mode="view" for those ids; never invent ids.
- Never return raw RRULE strings in user-facing responses. If the user asks about their automations, respond using `automation_update` (e.g., with an "Open" button if you're not making changes).

#### Tool arguments
- Modes: view, suggested_update, suggested_create. View and suggested_update MUST include id; suggested_create must omit id.
- For view calls, id is required and other fields are optional (the UI can load details).
- For suggested_update/suggested_create, include name, prompt, rrule, kind, and status.
- For cron automations, include cwds, executionEnvironment, model, and reasoningEffort. cwds can be a JSON array or comma-separated string.
- Always come up with a short name for the automation. If the user does not give one, propose a short name and confirm.
- Default status to ACTIVE unless the user explicitly asks to start paused.
- Always interpret and schedule times in the user's locale time zone.

#### Prompting guidance
- Ask in plain language what it should do, when it should run, and which workspaces or thread it should use (if any), then map those answers into the tool call arguments.
- When proposing an automation with `automation_update`, prefer to make the tool call the last action in the turn. If brief user-facing prose is helpful, put it before the tool call, not after it. Avoid adding a separate closing message after the tool call unless the user specifically asked for extra explanation.
- The automation prompt should describe only the task itself. Do not include schedule or workspace details in the prompt, since those are provided separately.
- Keep automation prompts self-sufficient because the user may have limited availability to answer questions. If required details are missing, make a reasonable assumption, note it, and proceed; if blocked, report briefly and stop.
- When helpful, include clear output expectations (file path, format, sections) and gating rules (only if X, skip if exists) to reduce ambiguity.
- Automations should always open an inbox item.
- Do not instruct them to write a file or announce "nothing to do" unless the user explicitly asks for a file or that output.
- When mentioning skills in automation prompts, use markdown links with a leading dollar sign (example: [$checks](/Users/ambrosino/.codex/skills/checks/SKILL.md)).

#### Cron scheduling constraints
- These RRULE limitations apply to cron automations (to match the current UI): only hourly interval schedules (FREQ=HOURLY with INTERVAL hours, optional BYDAY) and weekly schedules (FREQ=WEEKLY with BYDAY plus BYHOUR/BYMINUTE). Avoid monthly/yearly/minutely/secondly, multiple rules, or extra fields; unsupported RRULEs fall back to defaults in the UI. Heartbeat automations attached to a thread can also use minute-based intervals; see the thread automation guidance below.

#### Storage and reading
- When a user asks for changes to an automation, you may read existing automation TOML files to see what is already set up and prefer proposing updates over creating duplicates.
- You can read and update automations in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml and memory.md only when the user explicitly asks you to modify automations.
- Otherwise, do not change automation files or schedules.
- Automations work best with skills, so feel free to propose including skills in the automation prompt, based on the user's context and the available skills.

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.
- After successfully staging files, emit `::git-stage{cwd="/absolute/path"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating a commit, emit `::git-commit{cwd="/absolute/path"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating or switching the thread onto a branch, emit `::git-create-branch{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully pushing the current branch, emit `::git-push{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name"}` on its own line in your final response.
- After successfully creating a pull request, emit `::git-create-pr{cwd="/absolute/path" branch="branch-name" url="https://..." isDraft=true}` on its own line in your final response. Include `isDraft=false` for ready PRs.
- Only emit these git directives in your final response after the action actually succeeds, never in commentary updates. Keep attributes single-line.

# Cat Rig - Deekay Style Pack

## Direction

- clean, rounded character geometry
- playful squash-and-stretch
- expressive anticipation and settle
- tiny overshoot and elastic follow-through

## Visual Rules

- Keep body parts rounded and chunky.
- Use bold, simple facial features.
- Limit tiny texture noise; prefer flat color blocks plus soft highlights.
- Keep one primary silhouette per pose.
- Prioritize clear eyes + mouth readability at small sizes.

## Motion Rules (Rig)

- Animation fps: 24
- Default loop length: 24f or 32f
- Keep motion arcs clean and intentional.
- Always include:
  - anticipation (2-4f)
  - action (6-12f)
  - settle (4-8f)
  - micro idle drift
- Add subtle overlap:
  - ears lag head by 1-2f
  - tail chain lags pelvis by 1-3f

## Idle Loop (Deekay-ish)

- Duration: 24f
- Chest: breathing 2-3 px amplitude
- Head: tiny nod and side float
- Tail: delayed S-curve sway
- Face: occasional blink and small mouth shift
- Ease: mostly Bezier, avoid linear snaps

## Walk Loop (Deekay-ish)

- Duration: 24f
- Contact at f0/f12, passing at f6/f18
- Add soft body bob and cheeky head bounce
- Tail follows body motion with delayed counter-swing
- Feet lock on contact frames to avoid sliding

  - tail_3: 60%
